title: 5 Qwilr alternatives that win on speed, AI, and CRM integration [2026]
summary: Compare top Qwilr alternatives for B2B sales teams, focusing on speed, AI capabilities, and CRM integration to enhance proposal efficiency and engagement.
body_markdown:
*Disclaimer: This comparison is based on publicly available information and reflects GetAccept's independent view. Features, capabilities, pricing, and product scope* *are current as of March 2026 and may change over time.*


---


If you're searching for Qwilr alternatives, you're probably hitting one of these walls:


- You're spending days, not minutes, building each proposal - and there's no AI doing the heavy lifting, so you're still manually drafting in ChatGPT or Claude and copying the output back in.
- Your CRM shows a proposal was sent, but nothing useful after that - engagement data doesn't flow back in a way you can actually report on or act on.
- You have no idea when a deal's gone quiet and guessing whether to follow up.


We evaluated tools across three core dimensions - speed to create and send, depth of AI capabilities, and quality of CRM integration - to help you choose the right candidate.

## Why trust us?


We built GetAccept 10 years ago to solve a problem we saw playing out in B2B sales teams every day: proposals go out, and then nothing. No visibility into who read what, no way to engage the buying committee, no clear path from "proposal sent" to "deal closed."


That context shapes how we evaluate tools. We're looking at whether a platform helps reps spend less time on admin and more time closing. The research in this article draws from vendor documentation, public pricing pages, and verified user reviews on G2. Where review data wasn't available, we say so directly rather than filling the gap with assumptions.


## What is Qwilr?


Qwilr is a[proposal software](https://www.getaccept.com/blog/what-is-proposal-software) platform that lets sales teams create web-based, interactive documents instead of static PDFs.


The platform's core appeal is design quality. Proposals built in Qwilr look modern and branded, with interactive pricing tables, embedded videos, and accept/decline buttons built in. It integrates with CRMs including HubSpot and Salesforce, and offers basic engagement tracking so reps know when a proposal has been opened.


## Why teams consider Qwilr alternatives?


Qwilr makes proposals look great. But once you're actually using it day to day, three gaps tend to show up.


### 1. Building each proposal still takes too long.


Qwilr has no native AI to speak of - you're still drafting content elsewhere (ChatGPT, Claude) and pasting it in. What should take minutes after a call takes days.


### 2. Engagement data doesn't make it back to your CRM in a useful way.


You can pull deal data into a proposal, but what happens after - who opened it, what they did - doesn't flow back into your CRM in a way you can actually report on or act on.


### 3. You're often guessing why a deal's gone quiet.


A proposal sent is not the same as a deal moving. Without a clear signal that a room's gone cold, follow-up becomes a "just checking in" email instead of a well-timed nudge.


We evaluated tools across three dimensions — speed to create and send, depth of AI, and quality of CRM integration — to give you a clear picture of what's actually available in 2026.

## 2. Better Proposals


Best for


: Small to midsize sales teams, agencies, and service businesses that need a fast, affordable proposal tool with built-in e-signatures and payment collection.


Built for speed and simplicity, Better Proposals helps sales teams, agencies, and service businesses get professional proposals out the door fast - without a heavy implementation process or a steep learning curve. The platform combines proposal creation, legally binding e-signatures, and payment collection in a single workflow.


### Key features


- Interactive pricing tables that let buyers configure their own quotes within the proposal


- Legally binding digital signatures built directly into the proposal flow - no external e-sign tool required


- Payment integrations to collect payment at the point of acceptance, reducing the gap between signature and revenue


- Content library for storing and reusing approved proposal blocks, messaging, and assets


- Engagement notifications to alert reps when a proposal has been opened or interacted with


### Pros


- Public pricing is transparent and accessible, with a low starting price that makes it easy to evaluate without a sales call


- The combination of proposals, e-signatures, and payment collection in one tool reduces friction for teams closing smaller, faster deals


- Positioned squarely around speed - the product is designed to get proposals out quickly, which fits high-velocity sales motions


- A content library helps teams maintain consistency across proposals without starting from scratch each time


### Cons


- Available research does not confirm native CRM integrations, so fit for CRM-centric sales teams is unclear - verify this directly with the vendor before committing


- AI proposal generation capabilities are not documented in available sources, making it a weaker choice for teams prioritizing AI-assisted content creation


- The tool appears optimized for simpler, faster deal cycles - teams managing complex, multi-stakeholder B2B deals may find it limiting


### Pricing


- Starter: $13/user/month (billed annually), or $19/user/month billed monthly


- A free trial is available; additional tiers (including Premium) are listed on the vendor's pricing page


## 3. Proposify


Best for


: Small to mid-sized sales teams that want an affordable proposal tool with CRM integrations, and larger organizations that need approval workflows, SSO, and API access.


Proposify is a proposal and contract management platform built for sales teams that need more structure and process control than a basic document builder provides. Where some tools prioritize design flexibility, Proposify leans into workflow - CRM-connected proposals, approval routing, and document automation that helps teams standardize how deals get closed.


### Key features


- CRM integrations on the Team plan, including HubSpot and Pipedrive, to connect proposal workflows directly to your sales pipeline


- Unlimited document sends and custom fields for personalizing proposals at volume without manual rework


- Advanced approval workflows and conditional routing on the Business plan for organizations that need controlled review before proposals go out


- Unlimited e-signatures on the Basic plan, so teams can close deals without hitting signing limits


- Multiple workspaces and SSO on the Business plan for larger teams managing proposals across divisions or regions


### Pros


- Public pricing makes it easy to compare plans and estimate total cost without a demo requirement at the entry level


- The Team plan includes CRM integrations and automation, which is valuable for sales teams that want proposals connected to their pipeline data


- Higher-tier plans offer API access, SSO, and multiple workspaces - features that matter for scaling teams with more complex requirements


### Cons


- The Business plan starts at $3,900/year with a 10-user minimum, which is a significant jump in cost for smaller teams that need advanced features


- API access and SSO are locked to the highest tier, meaning teams that need deeper integrations have to pay for the full Business plan to get there


- No confirmed free plan in available sources - teams looking to test before committing may need to rely on a trial period


### Pricing


- Basic: $19/user/month (billed annually), or $29/month billed monthly


- Team: $41/user/month (billed annually), or $49/month billed quarterly


- Business: Starts at $3,900/year, typically with a minimum of 10 users


## 4. PandaDoc


Best for


: Sales, RevOps, and customer-facing teams in small to mid-sized businesses that need a fast, CRM-connected document automation platform for proposals, quotes, and contracts.


PandaDoc is one of the most recognized names in document automation. The platform covers proposals, quotes, contracts, and e-signatures in a single system, with CRM integrations that connect document workflows to your sales pipeline. It's a strong choice for teams that need to produce and manage a high volume of sales documents without building a patchwork of separate tools.


### Key features


- Drag-and-drop document editor with pre-built templates for fast proposal and quote creation without starting from scratch


- Pricing tables and CPQ capabilities for structured quoting that can be configured to match different deal types


- CRM integrations with Salesforce and HubSpot to connect documents with pipeline data and reduce manual data entry


- Approval workflows to route documents for internal review before they go to buyers


- Content library for storing and reusing approved sales assets, messaging, and legal language


- Built-in e-signatures for closing deals directly within the document, without moving to a separate signing tool


### Pros


- The free plan includes electronic signatures and document uploads, making it accessible for teams that want to test the tool before committing to a paid tier


- Built-in quoting, pricing tables, and CPQ capabilities make it a broader alternative to pure proposal tools


- Approval workflows help larger teams maintain quality control without slowing down the entire proposal process


### Cons


- PandaDoc is primarily a document platform - it doesn't offer Digital Sales Rooms, stakeholder-level engagement tracking, or Mutual Action Plans for managing the full buying committee experience


- AI features are largely in closed beta as of late 2025, with no public disclosure of the underlying model provider or where data is processed - a potential concern for teams with data residency requirements


- Advanced workflow and integration capabilities are gated to higher tiers, which may push smaller teams into plans that exceed their budget


### Pricing


- Free: $0 - electronic signatures, document uploads, up to 60 documents per year


- Starter: $19/user/month (billed annually), or $35/month billed monthly


- Business: $49/user/month (billed annually), or $65/month billed monthly


- Enterprise: Custom pricing - contact the vendor for a quote


## 5. DealHub.io


Best for


: Mid-market and enterprise revenue teams - particularly sales, RevOps, and deal desk leaders - who need faster quoting, approval automation, and CRM-connected CPQ and CLM workflows in a single platform.


DealHub.io takes a different angle than most tools on this list. Rather than starting with proposals and adding quoting as a feature, DealHub is built from the ground up as a quote-to-revenue platform - combining Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ), contract lifecycle management (CLM), and approval automation in a single system. It's aimed squarely at mid-market and enterprise revenue teams where pricing complexity, deal desk involvement, and approval chains are everyday realities.


### Key features


- CPQ capabilities to generate accurate quotes faster, even for complex product and pricing structures


- Automated approval workflows to reduce manual deal desk steps and accelerate quote-to-cash timelines


- Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) integrated into the same platform as quoting, reducing handoff friction between sales and legal


- CRM-connected workflows designed to tie quoting and contract activity back to your sales pipeline


### Pros


- Combining CPQ, CLM, and quote-to-revenue workflows in one system is a meaningful advantage for teams that currently manage these processes across separate tools


- Approval automation reduces the manual coordination that slows down deals when pricing exceptions or legal review are involved


- Positioned for enterprise sales operations where pricing complexity and governance requirements go beyond what proposal tools can handle


### Cons


- Pricing is not publicly listed, which makes it difficult to evaluate fit without going through a sales process - a friction point for teams doing early-stage research


- No G2 review evidence was available in the research for this article, so reviewer-validated strengths and weaknesses cannot be confirmed here


- The platform's depth in CPQ and CLM may be more than smaller teams need - it's a heavier implementation than a proposal-first tool


### Pricing


Pricing is not publicly listed - contact the vendor for a quote.


## Choosing the right Qwilr alternative


The right tool depends on what's actually slowing your deals down. Here's a quick guide to match your situation to the right pick:


- If your biggest problem is deal visibility after the proposal goes out


- you need to know who's reading what, which stakeholders are involved, and when to follow up -[GetAccept](https://app.getaccept.com/signup) is built for exactly this. No other tool on this list gives you stakeholder-level engagement data tied to a full Digital Sales Room experience.


- **If you need fast, affordable proposals with e-signatures and payment collection and your deals are relatively straightforward** , Better Proposals is worth a look. It's the most accessible option on price and setup time.


- **If you need CRM-connected proposals with approval workflows** and you're managing a team that needs more process control, Proposify is a solid mid-market choice - especially if HubSpot or Pipedrive is your CRM of record.


- **If document volume is your challenge** - you're producing a lot of proposals, quotes, and contracts and need automation to keep up - PandaDoc's document automation depth and free starting tier make it a practical option.


- **If pricing complexity and deal desk involvement are your daily reality** , and you need CPQ and CLM in one system, DealHub.io is the most purpose-built option for that use case.
